note: STAGE PERSONA graph. All fields describe the performer-as-acted, never the private person. No verbatim set text stored here. Fingerprints ≤7 words. 0 sets measured in repo — every field is authored hypothesis from widely-known public persona until word-timed sets are ingested.

identity.deal: Street philosopher who tells you the thing everyone in the room knows and nobody says, then holds the silence until the knowing becomes the laugh.
identity.premise: The smartest guy in the block party who happened to also read the books, telling the truth about race, fame, and the game in a voice that sounds like home.
identity.awareness_note: Hyper-aware of the room, the era, and his own position — the awareness is part of the performance, not behind it. He narrates his own footing ('I shouldn't say this') which IS the transgression framing.

philosophy.ontology: The world is a negotiation between what happened and who gets to tell it.
philosophy.epistemology: Everybody already knows; the comedy is in the saying, not the informing.
philosophy.axiology: Honesty about the game beats moralizing about the players.
philosophy.causality: Power writes the first draft; laughter edits it.
philosophy.agency: One comic with a mic can flip who's the被告 and who's the jury for one room at a time.

dramatic_core.want: the room to laugh at the truth before it can flinch from it
dramatic_core.fear: becoming the thing he's mocking — the preachy legend, the disconnected star
dramatic_core.need: one story that makes the powerful look small without him looking bitter
dramatic_core.self_model: the block's designated truth-teller who took the long way around

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats every uncomfortable social truth as a story-shaped object — if it can be narrated with the right character voices and the right pause, the room will indict itself without him ever stating the verdict.

identity.style_thesis: Philosophical-raconteur engine: treats every story as a parable with a moral he almost didn't notice. The character voices are both escape and exposure — he becomes other people to say the true thing. The hold after the heavy point is where the room catches up to what he actually said.

engine.archetype_def: sincere_storyteller per archetypes.json — self-deprecating adjacent but Chappelle's version is communal not self-directed; the sincerity is for the story, not the confession. Engine fit: sage_narrator, warm_mother low-tempo.
engine.archetype_delivery: mid pitch, wide dynamics, build-then-collapse structure, comfort with silence — matches his hold-after-heavy-point signature

mary_coords.status: no measured modulator; likely mid-arousal wide-valence swing (heavy stories land at low valence, the laughter release at positive)

set_queue.note: 0 sets measured. First ingest should be a storytelling-era special (Killin Them Softly, For What It's Worth, The Age of Spin) — the raconteur engine at full power. Need word-timed ASR; the hold-after-point timing hypothesis is the thing to measure first.

timing_profile.hypothesis: sprints in character voices (fast, wide dynamics) then HOLDS on the heavy point (long silence after the turn, often 2-3s+) — the room does the indicting in the silence. Different from Louis (confessional dead-stop) and Norm (never-stop): Chappelle's stop is the sermon's altar call, timed so the room preaches to itself.
stop_start: start: character voice sprint, the story running hot
stop: the narrator steps out, the point lands
hold: silence while the room catches up to what it just agreed with
start: next character, the story resumes like nothing happened
timing_profile.doctrine_hypothesis: Sprints in character, holds 2-3s+ after heavy point. The hold after the heavy point is the signature — the room needs the silence to metabolize what he just said. The story sermon: he tells it like it happened to someone he knew, then reveals it happened to all of us.

gtvh_profile.SO: normal/absurd — but social: the normal IS the absurd once narrated from the outside position
gtvh_profile.LM: double_interpret + status_invert — every story runs on a double meaning (what happened vs. who it happens to) and the laugh flips who's on top
gtvh_profile.TA: powerful / peers / social groups — punches at systems and in-group dynamics; when he targets the self it's to disarm, not to confess
gtvh_profile.NS: anecdote / character-chain — story-form with multiple character voices inside one narrative

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.

essay_seeds.title: Why is Dave Chappelle funny? The philosophical raconteur engine
essay_seeds.thesis: Treats every uncomfortable social truth as a story-shaped object — if it can be narrated with the right character voices and the right pause, the room will indict itself without him ever stating the verdict.
outline: what makes this persona impossible to copy

essay_seeds.title: Dave Chappelle: 'The story that turns' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: Tells a story with the cadence of a folktale, then the turn reveals the story was about something larger (race, power, America). garden_path: the room thinks it's a story, it's actually a thesis. The hold after the turn is the room metabolizing the double meaning.
outline: what this reveals about the engine

essay_seeds.title: Dave Chappelle: 'The character as a shield and a weapon' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: Becomes a character to say the thing he couldn't say as himself. The character is the benign frame; the content is the violation. The room laughs at the character and absorbs the thesis at the same time.
outline: what this reveals about the engine
